refs.title: Hail to the Queen! - Pennsylvania Historic Preservation (Pennsylvania State Historic Preservation Office)
refs.note: Added 5 Sep 2026 when queen-anne-american and queen-anne-free-classic were linked to this record. Its own words: 'The first Queen Anne style building in America is considered to be the Watts Sherman house designed by Henry Hobson Richardson and built in 1874 in Newport, Rhode Island. Featuring heavily textured, shingled wall surfaces, prominent brick chimneys and intersecting gables, it was most faithful to the designs promoted by Shaw and other English architects. Due to its shingled walls, the Watts Sherman house is also seen as an early example of the Shingle style' -- a state preservation office saying in one paragraph why three nodes of this corpus all name the same building. Note that it dates the house 1874 where this record's survey and Wikipedia say 1875-1876.

quotes.text: 2. Foundations: The stone foundations have irregular coursing-. There are some interior walls, and chimney foundations of brick.
quotes.page: HABS No. RI-342, Part II.B.2; same span

quotes.text: 3. Wall construction: The basement and first story walls are of pink granite random ashlar. The drip molding, window sills, mullions, corners and wall intersections are pecked and rusti- cated reddish sandstone. Red mortar with a projecting half- round accents the pattern of the masonry. There are two brownstone columns with abstracted capitals. The upper stories are framed with half timbering stucco, and various forms of cut shingles.
quotes.page: HABS No. RI-342, Part II.B.3; same span

quotes.text: k. Structural system; The first story is masonry with upper stories of woodem framing and. heavy studding. . Interior partitions are wooden framed with heavy studding.

quotes.text: b. Windows: In the original portion of the house, the windows are generally in groups of two, three, five or singular units. On the first floor they are usually double hung with fixed transom above of either stained glass or tinted, textured glass.

Shape and covering: Steep gable roofs, originally covered with wooden shingles laid in horizontal patterns with periodic rows of decoratively cut forms, are now covered with asphalt shingles Decorated barge boards terminate the gable...ends- with molded cornices and bracketed eaves along the lower edge of the roofs. There is one dormer with a gable and several dormers with the roofs. The lower slope of the roofs are slightly splayed.

8. Porches, stoops and bulkheads: The low sloping roof of the porte- cocheVe is supported on chamfered posts. Decoratively cut shingles decorate the sides of the roof. Adjacent to the house are round arched openings with fixed windows and small lights.

note: The survey's own reading of the eave -- 'bracketed eaves along the lower edge of the roofs' -- is worth carrying against the shingle-style kit's canonical 'closed-tight-no-brackets' eave: this is the prototype, and the register calls it Queen Anne. Named by queen-anne-free-classic and queen-anne-american at the same location string, and linked to both on 5 Sep 2026 (WP-11.3, Queen Anne and Stick Style cluster) -- three nodes on one building, which is what the graph's multiple parentage here is for. For the free-classic node the survey's alteration line is the whole point: 'Stanford White, after his return from Europe in 18T9, remodeled the interior and en- larged the house to the east', so the vocabulary shift this subtype is about happened on this one building and is dated by a surveyor. Seeded 4 Sep 2026.
